hyps.why: Lowering an excessively high learning rate rescues diverging training, giving large gains.
Very small learning rates undertrain in 243 epochs, so raising them helps.
Strong L2 penalty underfits, so reducing it helps.
Deeper nets are more unstable at high learning rates, so removing a layer helps.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize high learning rate training.
Small batches with high learning rates are noisy, so lowering lr helps more.
Wider networks have larger effective step sizes and diverge more at high learning rates.
Increasing an already high learning rate causes divergence.
With low learning rates, weaker regularization lets the net fit more in limited epochs.
Adding layers at high learning rate worsens instability.
